title: Reviewing and Interpreting Cultural Works
summary: Presenting interpretations, supporting judgments with evidence, and responding to alternative readings.
whyItMatters: A strong review helps an audience understand both what a work attempts and how successfully its artistic choices achieve that purpose.

mentalModel.title: Observation, interpretation, evaluation
mentalModel.content: Move from a concrete detail to its possible meaning and then to a justified judgment.

mentalModel.title: Acknowledge alternatives
mentalModel.content: Present another plausible reading before explaining why your interpretation remains stronger or more useful.

ruleBlocks.title: Open with a focused judgment
ruleBlocks.content: Name the work, its central concern, and your main evaluation without recounting the whole plot.

ruleBlocks.title: Anchor claims in details
ruleBlocks.content: Refer to scenes, language, structure, visual choices, performance, or sound.

ruleBlocks.title: Respond to other readings fairly
ruleBlocks.content: Use reported speech, identify common ground, and locate the exact point of disagreement.

tables.title: Review and Discussion Toolkit
rows: Die Szene lässt sich als ... deuten.
Die Regisseurin betont, der Film sei ...

examples.de: Der Roman überzeugt vor allem dort, wo er private Entscheidungen mit politischen Folgen verbindet.
examples.en: The novel is most convincing where it connects private decisions with political consequences.

examples.de: Dafür spricht das wiederkehrende Bild der geschlossenen Tür.
examples.en: The recurring image of the closed door supports this interpretation.

examples.de: Einige Kritiker meinen, das Ende sei zu offen; gerade diese Offenheit zwingt das Publikum jedoch zu einer eigenen Position.
examples.en: Some critics say the ending is too open; however, that openness forces the audience to take its own position.

commonMistakes.wrong: Use positive or negative adjectives without evidence.
commonMistakes.correct: Connect every major judgment to a formal or thematic detail.

commonMistakes.wrong: Dismiss another interpretation as simply wrong.
commonMistakes.correct: State its evidence before identifying its limits.
commonMistakes.reason: Interpretive discussions rarely have only one possible reading.

comparisons.summary: The theme provides analytical categories for form, context, representation, and reception.
